purpose: Cross-check the 12 binomial labels in the 2019 Lake Oro/Lake Dakong Napo FishTaxa paper against Eschmeyer’s Catalog of Fishes, without rewriting the historical paper labels or claiming specimen re-identification.

independentAuthority.name: Eschmeyer’s Catalog of Fishes
independentAuthority.publisher: California Academy of Sciences, Institute for Biodiversity Science and Sustainability
independentAuthority.entryVersionCaveat: The indexed individual fish-name records used here displayed older page headers (13 August or 21 September 2026). A per-entry update date for the 20 October overview version was not verified.
independentAuthority.access: Individual Catalog pages could not be opened normally during this review (HTTP 403/502); exact-name indexed excerpts from the official Catalog pages were used. No access challenge was bypassed.
independentAuthority.license: No item-specific open license or permission to republish Catalog text was identified. This audit records short attributed name-status results only; it does not reproduce Catalog entries.

comparativeEvidence.note: Eschmeyer’s Catalog treats Trichogaster trichopterus as a synonym of Trichopodus trichopterus, matching the article’s own Table 2 combination. Clarias batrachus is valid as printed in the checked Catalog record; do not replace it with Clarias magur. The catalog’s range note for C. batrachus is contextual and does not resolve the lake specimens.

limitations: An accepted name does not verify an author’s identification of an individual sample or resolve the mixed collected-or-purchased provenance.
The catalog crosswalk does not establish a current presence in either lake, population status, native/introduced status for this particular sample, catchability, diet, safety or fishing legality.
The study’s all-rights-reserved statement remains separate from factual nomenclatural normalization; no source occurrence row or article table is licensed by this crosscheck.
The Catalog’s page update dates vary across the selected indexed records; only the overall project page reports a 20 October 2026 version.
nextAction: Search bounded, independently reusable specimen or occurrence records for the two lake localities; retain the study’s 2017 table as historical context until collection provenance and rights are resolved.
